plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to zero.

conservative.read: This plan prioritizes capital preservation with a target of around 1.5% monthly growth. It significantly reduces risk by cutting all leveraged ETFs and high-beta single names, aiming for lower drawdowns.

plan: Trim leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU) to small positions.
Reduce AI/Software leveraged positions (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to smaller sizes.
Buy OXY as a new, high-scoring long setup.
Maintain a blend of broad index, quality tech, and some leverage.

balanced.read: This balanced approach targets about 2.5% monthly growth by managing risk first. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while adding a promising new name, aiming for steady growth with moderate drawdowns.

plan: Increase exposure to AI/Software leveraged ETFs (METU, MSFU, PLTU).

aggressive.read: This aggressive plan aims for high growth, targeting around 4% monthly, by leaning into leverage and concentration. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and promising setups, but this comes with substantially higher risk, potential for large drawdowns, and the impact of daily leveraged ETF decay.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs and AI/Software leveraged positions.
Increase QQQI to 30% to maximize income generation.

income.read: This income-focused plan targets around 1% monthly distributions by shifting to income-generating ETFs like QQQI. It drastically cuts leverage and high-beta single names to prioritize stability and reliable income, accepting lower growth potential and still acknowledging NAV risk in market downturns.
